newsitem.title: USA: Northern Telecom sets '97 revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: Northern Telecom sets '97 revenue growth.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd's vice-president of investor relations R.B. Kaye said the company was targeting revenue growth in the "mid-teens" for 1997 and gross margins of around 40 percent.
"We intend to have return on assets of between 16 and 19 percent" this year, he told investors in a presentation at the Robertson Stephens technology conference.

Kaye said Nortel expected general sales and administration costs in the 17-19 percent range and that research and development should be in the 12-14 percent of revenue range. Strong investment was a requirement to remain competitive in the telecommunications equipment business, he added.
Kaye said he also expected measurements of customer satisfaction, the basis for a significant portion of senior management compensation, would be over 85 percent.

Nortel has enjoyed rapid growth in its wireless network products, which approached 20 percent of total revenue in 1996. Data and media communications, have grown substantially since its launch into the categories in 1994, Kaye added.
He also noted surveys had estimated overall infrastructure revenue growth would rise from $560 billion last year to $7.3 billion in 2000.
